title: Kernel and cokernel computation of a diagonal identity block
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and X,Y,U,C be A-modules. Let f:X→Y and g:A→C be linear, eX:X≃U×A and eY:Y≃U×C linear equivalences. Assume eY(f(x))=((eX(x)).1,g((eX(x)).2)) for every x. Then ker g≃ker f and Y/range f≃C/range g as A-modules. No finiteness, freeness or local-ring condition is needed.

source.place: Tag 00O0, residual-block quotient argument; Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Isomorphisms, LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective.

proof.text: Map a∈ker g to eX⁻¹(0,a). The diagonal identity and injectivity of eY show this lies in ker f. Conversely x∈ker f has (eX x).1=0 and g((eX x).2)=0. Last-coordinate projection is the inverse. These maps preserve addition and scalars.

Let q:Y→C/range g be y↦[(eY y).2]. It is onto because [(c)] has preimage eY⁻¹(0,c). If q(y)=0, write (eY y).2=g(a); then y=f(eX⁻¹((eY y).1,a)) by the diagonal identity. Conversely q(f(x))=0. Thus ker q=range f, and quotient transport followed by LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective gives the cokernel equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem residue_kernel_unit_minor_quotient
    (A : Type v) [CommRing A] (X Y U C : ModuleCat.{v} A)
    (f : X →ₗ[A] Y) (g : A →ₗ[A] C)
    (eX : X ≃ₗ[A] (U × A)) (eY : Y ≃ₗ[A] (U × C))
    (hdiag : ∀ x, eY (f x) = ((eX x).1, g (eX x).2)) :
    Nonempty (LinearMap.ker g ≃ₗ[A] LinearMap.ker f) ∧
      Nonempty ((Y ⧸ LinearMap.range f) ≃ₗ[A] (C ⧸ LinearMap.range g))
